items.title: Xiquelene Market fire enters day 3 in Maputo as firefighters await power cut to resume operations — Miramar
items.summary: Images captured at the scene by the Miramar team show dozens of stalls and warehouses destroyed, many of which housed highly flammable products. Stall owners report substantial financial losses and are facing serious difficulties moving around inside the market, where water used during the initial firefighting operations has turned the ground into a muddy pool Despite the initial intervention by the National Public Rescue Service (SENSAP), firefighters were unable to completely extinguish the flames. According to the affected vendors, the firefighters temporarily suspended operations and are awaiting a team from Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) to cut off the electricity supply. The measure is intended to ensure safety before firefighting operations resume to definitively extinguish the blaze, as “water and electricity do not mix”

items.title: Mozambique: Marracuene imposes security restrictions on access to Macaneta Beach — Watch
items.summary: To prevent a repeat of the unrest witnessed last weekend, vehicle access on public holidays and long weekends will now be restricted. Only the first 150 vehicles will be allowed to cross and park in the authorised parking area. Other visitors will have to leave their cars in Marracuene town and continue by buses provided by the municipal authorities, at a fare of 15 meticais per journey. Children up to the age of 10 travel free The new rules, presented at a press conference on Monday, also provide for strict checks before and after the toll booth, including mandatory breathalyser tests for drivers and thorough searches to confiscate glass bottles, alcoholic drinks and sharp objects The consumption and sale of alcohol are strictly prohibited on the beach, in car parks and on public roads, and are permitted only inside licensed hotels, lodges and restaurants.

items.title: Religious faiths crucial for peace promotion
items.summary: Maputo, 29 Sep (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo calls on religious faiths to be engaged in promotion of ethical and moral values as they are important partners in building a more peaceful society. The President, speaking on Monday in Matola, southern province of Maputo, at the opening of the 9th National Religious Conference, explained that the more people are aware of morality, moral values and ethical principles, the fewer people the country would have in prison. Chapo believed that preventing social problems should begin with the moral education of citizens from childhood and the fight against corruption must be accompanied by the education of upright citizens capable of contributing to the construction of a society based on ethical values and peaceful coexistence.

items.title: Morocco: King appoints first woman prime minister
items.summary: The appointment of Fatima Zahra Mansouri comes after her center-right party won last week's parliamentary elections in Morocco. She had previously served as mayor of the city of Marrakesh Fatima Zahra Mansouri became Morocco 's first female prime minister, the country's royal cabinet announced on Tuesday. King Mohammed VI has tasked her with forming the next government Under the Moroccan constitution, the country's king has the power to appoint the prime minister, but he must choose someone from the party that wins the most seats in parliamentary elections Mansouri's appointment comes after her center-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) won last week's parliamentary elections PAM raked in 97 out of 395 seats in the House of Representatives, 31 more than the next closest competitor. The vote was, however, marred by the lowest turnout in two decades "For the first time in our country's history, a woman is taking on the responsibility of leading the government," Mansouri said.

items.title: TV journalist is crowned king of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom
items.summary: Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has ascended to the throne after King Oyo died at the age of 34 due to a cancer battle. He previously worked for Ugandan broadcaster UBC as a TV anchor and editor A TV journalist on Tuesday was crowned king of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom Edward Rukidi Kiganangoma has ascended to the thrown after his predecessor, King Oyo Kyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, died unexpectedly last month King Oyo was only 34 and had lost his cancer battle while receiving treatment in the US. Oyo had became king at only three years of age Oyo's death sparked a succession battle in Uganda , with Oyo's mother pushing for the late king's undisclosed son to be the next monarch However, the royal Babito clan chose Kiganangoma, now Nyabongo I, as the heir to the throne out of a group of eligible princes Kiganangoma took part in a coronation ceremony in the remote town of Fort Portal in western Uganda to ascend to the throne Coronation rituals included a mock battle and animal sacrifices.

items.title: Three Egyptian security officials convicted of kidnapping Italian student
items.summary: Three members of the Egyptian security forces have been convicted by a Rome court for being involved in kidnapping Italian student Giulio Regeni Three Egyptian security officials have been convicted by a Rome court over the kidnapping of an Italian student whose tortured body was found in Cairo a decade ago The men, who were tried in absentia, denied the charges. On Monday they were sentenced to 10 years in prison on charges of aggravated kidnapping. A fourth Egyptian defendant was acquitted Giulio Regeni, 28, was studying for a doctorate at Cambridge University when he went missing while on a research trip in Egypt in 2016 Days later, his mutilated body was found in a ditch near Cairo.
